answer: Each identity must store a unique 100 MB shard and lock 30 POA, then answer a retrieval challenge within 10 minutes each epoch; a failed proof forfeits the deposit. Shards derive from the identity key, so one disk cannot serve many identities: like a lantern lighting only its own corner of a nebula, each fake needs its own storage and bandwidth. An attacker running 100 fakes must store 10 GB and answer 100 unpredictable challenges, while a comet of quick copies fails because duplicate shards share the same proof. Verifiers issue random chunk requests and check Merkle proofs on-chain.
